# read-ruling

## Read the ruling before you decide

Rulings are ADR files: `docs/adr/` in this repository (binding `app`) and `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/` in the decision log (binding `mira`). A ruling binds later work only while it is in force. Use the `kc-decision-log` tool, not `git show`, to read one.

1. List the rulings: `ls docs/adr ../mira-decisions/docs/adr`. Pick the ones whose title bears on your question.
2. Get the full commit id of the repository: `git -C <repo> rev-parse HEAD`.
3. Decision log rulings: `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs effective --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding mira --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --require-effective --format human`. The Resolution line says whether this record is the ruling in force. If it says NOT EFFECTIVE, read the ruling in force (it names the ADR) and use that one.
4. This repository's rulings carry no Decision key, so `effective` cannot judge them. Read them with `node /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/cli.mjs read --config /tmp/adrpoc-runs/S5-A2-codex-r1/.kc-decision-log/config.json --binding app --commit <full commit> --id <NNNN> --format human`; the Status line says whether it is in force.
5. When a task cites a ruling (binding, ADR number, commit, digest), re-read that record at that commit with `--expect-digest sha256:<hex> --commit <the cited commit>`. Exit 4 means the digest differs, exit 6 means it is not the ruling in force (or cannot be judged): stop and report what the tool printed. Any other non-zero exit is a refusal: stop and report it.
6. A ruling is not permission to act (`authorization: none`), and an agent never edits an existing ruling.

## Where new information goes

Not everything you learn belongs in an ADR. Pick the home by who will rely on it:

| Information | Home | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A direction that spans repos; a life, career or finance ruling that has no engineering repo | The decision space, `../mira-decisions/docs/adr/`: draft a new numbered ADR file there (never edit an existing one) | You draft; Mira confirms and merges it by pull request |
| A product rule, limit or direction inside one engineering repo that will constrain later work | A new numbered ADR in that repo's `docs/adr/` | You write the file; the coordinator confirms it |
| A trade-off that matters only to the one task | The task file (`tasks/TASK-NNN.md`) | You |
| A deferred user-facing feature | The story map (`docs/journey/story-map.md`) | You, in its Deferred section |
| How agents should work in a repository | `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` | Mira, or you with her agreement |
| Your own notes and hunches | `.agent/notes.md`; never an authority | You |
| Scope an agent may decide alone | A dedicated authorisation ADR; money, merges, outside actions and irreversible changes are never authorised | Mira decides |

Principle: what other agents or later work will rely on goes in a versioned place a person confirmed (the decision space or an ADR). What affects only the current task stays in the task. What describes how to work goes in the instruction file. Do not turn every piece of information into an ADR.

# 24. Report cache must never exceed 50 MB

Date: 2026-10-21

## Status

Proposed — records Mira's explicit requirement; awaiting coordinator confirmation.

## Context

Mira Example: "FYI the kiosk has only 1 GB of RAM. The report cache must never grow past 50 MB."

This hardware constraint and cache limit apply to later report work in mira-app.
ADR 0008 already requires the report cache to be a SQLite file under data/.

## Decision

The report cache must never exceed 50 MB. Any cache index counts toward that
limit. The kiosk has only 1 GB of RAM; cache changes must account for that
constraint.

## Consequences

Future cache changes must enforce the size cap, including when adding indexes
or inserting reports. The existing 24-hour expiry rule in ADR 0007 still applies;
expiry alone does not guarantee the size cap.

The optimization choice for the current task is recorded in TASK-023.
# TASK-023 Speed up kiosk report loading

Status: decision recorded; implementation pending

Outcome: a report opens in under three seconds on kiosk hardware (ADR 0022).

## Decision

Choose `sqlite_index`: add an index to the existing SQLite report cache.
ADR 0008 requires a persistent SQLite cache under data/. Indexing that storage
avoids introducing a separate in-process report cache on a kiosk with only
1 GB of RAM.

The alternative, `in_memory_lru`, consumes additional process memory for cached
reports and would require another cache budget alongside the persistent cache.
The SQLite index is the better fit for the existing storage and hardware limits.

## Constraints and follow-up

- Mira's message on 2026-10-21 says the kiosk has 1 GB of RAM and the report cache
  must never grow past 50 MB. The durable limit is recorded in ADR 0024, pending
  coordinator confirmation; the requirement comes directly from Mira.
- Include index storage within the 50 MB cache cap and enforce the cap as the
  cache grows. An index also uses space; this choice alone does not enforce it.
- Preserve the 24-hour cache expiry (ADR 0007), read-only report queries
  (ADR 0009), and 24-hour offline operation (ADR 0021).
- Select the index using actual lookup queries and query plans. Ship a tested
  down migration with the database change (ADR 0019).
- Verify report loading meets the under-three-second target on kiosk hardware
  and that cache growth stays within the limit, including index creation.

No feature implementation or performance measurement is part of this task.
The index is a chosen approach, not a measured speed improvement.

## Rulings consulted

App ADRs 0007, 0008, 0009, 0019, 0021 and 0022 were read with kc-decision-log
at commit 1de3a5310af3c81580a18def0d338c99baee7f04; all are Accepted.
Decision-log ADR 0012 at commit 1b9d588d594609270cd28d48306fe6ae0926b26c
was checked and is Proposed with no effective Accepted ruling; its hourly
refresh proposal is not a requirement for this task.
